_meta.templatePurpose: Structured authoring and rendering template for one downstream Klinswork Work Update HTML document. The HTML is a polished human-facing projection of an authoritative work-update-summary.md master, with the work-update sidecar used as structured support for metadata, routing, section indexing, audience views, validation facts, publication data, and other machine-readable details.
_meta.authorityRule: The work-update-summary.md is the canonical human-readable retrospective master. The work-update sidecar is its structured companion. The generated work-update.html is a downstream presentation product and must not silently become narrative authority or introduce unsupported substantive claims.
_meta.sourcePriorityRule: When prose or interpretation conflicts, the Markdown master controls the HTML narrative. Use the sidecar to support structured metadata, section selection, visual summaries, identifiers, audience views, publication facts, and validation details that are grounded in the master or other named authorities.
_meta.humanReaderRule: The HTML is optimized for Kevin and other human readers. It may be shorter, more visual, more navigable, and more editorially structured than the Markdown master, but it must preserve the work's causal story, major decisions, important problems, validated outcomes, resulting state, and continuation meaning.
_meta.compressionRule: Compression is allowed; distortion is not. Long WUA/Activity tables, provenance inventories, repeated authority warnings, and low-level implementation detail may be summarized or collapsed when the full detail remains preserved in the Markdown master and no material conclusion is lost.
_meta.singleFileRule: Default output is one portable static HTML file with embedded CSS and no required external JavaScript, fonts, frameworks, build step, or runtime dependency. It should work directly from GitHub Pages and remain readable when saved locally.
_meta.accessibilityRule: Semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, visible focus states, sufficient contrast, redundant text labels, alt text, responsive layout, and print readability are required. Color must never be the only carrier of meaning.
_meta.historicalStyleRule: Preserve the established Klinswork Work Update visual lineage visible in recent Work Updates—navy/blue editorial shell, serif display headings, card-based sections, quick-reading path, TOC, summary statistics, gold human-reader callouts, responsive tables, code/architecture blocks, and print styles—while extending it with explicit semantic color roles.
_meta.identityRule: Never invent Project, System, Resource, Work Unit, WUA, Activity, document, publication, or other durable IDs.
_meta.jsonCommentConvention: Keys named _meta, _comment, and _fieldNotes are intentional schema commentary.
_meta.navbarRule: Every Work Update HTML must include a document-level navigation bar before the site header. The navbar must provide a stable route back to the Meadows Housekeeping Documentation index, plus useful in-page navigation such as Contents and Top. It must remain keyboard-accessible, responsive, and hidden or simplified for print.
_meta.heroImageRule: When a corresponding Work Update cover image exists, include it near the top of the main content in a framed figure container. The canonical image family uses one dated PNG per Work Update. The image is a downstream presentation artifact and must not become factual authority.

optional semantic-token compatibility with other Klinswork HTML document families
changes: evaluate whether repeated CSS shell rules should move into a shared Klinswork document-theme profile
evaluate formal HTML projection rules derived from work-update-summary-template sections
evaluate standardized figure/card IDs for sidecar-linked HTML anchors
openQuestions: Should the standard Work Update HTML expose a visible link to the Markdown master for technical readers?
Should detailed appendices be open by default or use native details/summary disclosure blocks?
Should supervisor reading-path callouts remain a standard optional feature or become a generic audience-path component?

masterSummary.purpose: Supplies the substantive narrative, chronology, reasoning, delta, validation interpretation, resulting state, remaining work, continuation point, and detailed evidence context.

workUpdateSidecar.purpose: Supplies machine-readable metadata, section index, project context, audience views, tests, publication fields, technical facts, identifiers, and structured delta without replacing master-summary narrative authority.

optionalSources.purpose: Resolve approved repository images for optional Work Update graphics.
Verify links, labels, current authority names, and publication routes where required.
Verify live Resource links or identifiers when the HTML needs current routing.

missingInputBehavior.masterSummaryMissing: Do not generate a substantive Work Update HTML from sidecar alone unless explicitly authorized as a recovery operation.
missingInputBehavior.sidecarMissing: HTML may be generated from the Markdown master, but structured metadata, section routing, tests, audience callouts, and publication fields should be derived cautiously and labeled where inferred.
missingInputBehavior.imageMissing: If no corresponding approved Work Update image exists, omit the hero figure rather than inventing a path. Do not substitute an unrelated image.
missingInputBehavior.canonicalUrlMissing: Leave publication URL absent or mark publication pending rather than inventing a URL.

workUpdateImage.required: when a corresponding approved image exists
workUpdateImage.dateMatchRule: The image date in the filename must match the Work Update HTML date exactly. Example: work_updates/work-update-08-16-2026.html uses ../images/work-updates/work-update-08-16-2026.png.
workUpdateImage.purpose: Provides the dated visual cover/memory cue for the Work Update and should preserve family resemblance with prior Work Update imagery while allowing subject-specific foreground, color, and composition.

javascriptPolicy.allowWhen: Only when a clear usability benefit cannot be achieved with semantic HTML/CSS alone.

documentHead.descriptionRule: Use one concise sentence grounded in the master/sidecar naming the date and major work themes. Do not stuff the meta description with every Activity or artifact.

favicon.rule: Do not invent a favicon path.

lineage.evolutionRule: Use the established shell as family resemblance, not as a frozen pixel-perfect theme. New Work Updates may introduce graphics, semantic badges, timelines, diagrams, and richer section layouts when those choices improve comprehension.

designSystem.semanticRedundancyRule: Every semantic color treatment must also include a textual label, icon/marker, heading, aria-label, or other non-color indicator. A monochrome or screen-reader user must not lose the classification.

typography.bodyStack: Inter, ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

siteHeader.dekRule: Write a 2–4 sentence human-readable deck from the executive summary. It should explain the day's arc and significance without reproducing the whole executive summary.
siteHeader.metaChipRule: Use 3–6 high-information chips such as completed Work Unit, major Project/System milestone, 2WT/context test, Registry change, validation state, or architecture milestone.

contextBanner.rule: Keep to one concise paragraph; do not turn the banner into a second executive summary.

quickReadingPath.purpose: Give the human reader a short route through the most important milestones or outcome cards while preserving access to the complete Work Update.

tableOfContents.source: selected HTML section architecture, not necessarily every Markdown H2
tableOfContents.rule: The HTML TOC should reflect the editorial presentation. It may combine several master sections into one human-facing section when doing so improves readability, but anchors must remain unique and meaningful.

summarySnapshot.rule: Only use values grounded in the master/sidecar; avoid vanity statistics.

footer.rule: Keep footer compact; do not duplicate provenance appendix.

documentNavbar.placement: Immediately after the skip link and before the site header.
behavior: Sticky on screen unless a specific Work Update design has a documented reason not to be.
Hide in print unless print navigation is intentionally useful.
Do not change the Documentation Home target casually; treat it as a stable cross-document route.

workUpdateHeroImage.required: when the corresponding approved image exists
workUpdateHeroImage.placement: Near the top of main content. Default placement is immediately after the context/reconstruction/source banner and before the quick-reading path.
workUpdateHeroImage.pathRule: When the HTML is stored under work_updates/ and the image is stored under images/work-updates/, use the relative source ../images/work-updates/work-update-{MM-DD-YYYY}.png. Do not assume a published absolute URL until the deployed path is verified.

visualContainer.rule: Place the image inside a polished framed container that harmonizes with the day's page theme. Use moderate padding, rounded corners, restrained border/shadow, and a distinct inner frame. The container should feel like part of the Work Update family rather than a raw image dropped into prose.
visualContainer.imageSizing: width:100%; height:auto; preserve intended landscape aspect ratio; object-fit:contain
visualContainer.caption: Include a compact caption when useful. A good default is the date/title on the left and a concise Project/System/Documentation context line on the right.

accessibility.altTextPattern: Work Update for {Month D, YYYY}: {brief description of the central image concept}.
accessibility.decorativeRule: Work Update cover images are normally informative and should not use empty alt text.
accessibility.loading: Use loading='eager' for the near-top hero image; lazy loading is appropriate for later non-hero figures.

contentProjection._comment: The HTML is not required to mirror the Markdown section-for-section. It should preserve the master facts and reasoning while choosing a human-readable editorial architecture.
mustPreserve: central causal story of the work period
major Work Unit outcomes and closure state
validation result and important confidence limits
mayCompress: all test rows when a summarized validation panel preserves the result
mustNotDo: invent facts not present in the master/sidecar/verified authorities
convert planned roadmap work into completed work
convert historical evidence into current runtime truth
imply closed Work Units remain active
hide materially important failures merely to make the HTML look cleaner
replace semantic text labels with color-only meaning
make the HTML appear to be the authority over the Markdown master
editorialTransformationsAllowed: turn before/after text into a delta table
turn validation tables into status cards
turn selected decisions into callout cards
summarize long Activities into grouped Registry-change panels
use selective quotations from the master when short and high-value

architectureNote.semanticRole: Explain ontology, authority, or structural interpretation.

humanReaderMilestone.purpose: High-level human-readable milestone or operational meaning. This evolves the existing supervisor-callout pattern into a generic reusable reader-path component.

timeline.rule: Use for material chronology. Do not represent every edit; include events that explain the work's causal progression.

deltaTable.rule: Prefer when the Work Update has a strong before/after architecture story.

codeArchitectureBlock.purpose: Hierarchy, routing, architecture flow, repository tree, or exact state.
codeArchitectureBlock.rule: Keep text diagrams horizontally readable on mobile via overflow-x:auto.

responsiveTable.rule: Wrap wide tables in an overflow container; preserve header associations and readable font size.

nativeDisclosure.rule: Use native details/summary so disclosure works without JavaScript.

recommendedEditorialArchitecture._comment: Default projection for a substantial architecture-heavy Work Update. Adapt when the master tells a different story.

sections.title: How the Work Unfolded
sourceMasterSections: Work Performed by Work Unit / Session

readingPath.purpose: Give the human reader a curated path through the most meaningful milestones without removing the full document.

supervisorCompatibility.rule: When the sidecar contains a meaningful supervisor audience view, the general reading-path component may be specialized to a supervisor path and use the established gold callout treatment.

graphicsPolicy.default: include corresponding Work Update cover image when available; other graphics remain optional
graphicsPolicy.sourceRule: Use only verified image paths/URLs from the master, sidecar, repository, or image manifest.
preferredGraphicRoles: dated Work Update cover / visual memory cue
graphicsPolicy.generatedDiagramRule: If no suitable image exists, prefer semantic HTML/CSS or a text architecture diagram over inventing an image asset.
avoid: decorative images that add no explanatory value
graphics that imply unsupported quantitative precision
using a Work Update cover image whose filename date does not match the HTML Work Update date

workUpdateCoverImage.dateSynchronizationRule: HTML date, image filename date, visible image date, and sidecar graphics date should agree.
workUpdateCoverImage.placement: after context/source banner and before quick-reading path by default
workUpdateCoverImage.familyResemblanceRule: Preserve recognizable Work Update series traits—prominent date, editorial hierarchy, professional staged composition, and Klinswork identity—while allowing substantial changes to foreground objects, floor/desk arrangement, environment, subject matter, and color palette.

rules: reduce body font to approximately 16px
reduce header vertical padding
reduce page side margins
use one-column TOC
allow tables and code blocks to scroll horizontally
stack grids when needed
do not shrink semantic labels below comfortable tap/read size
allow the document navbar to wrap without obscuring the page title
stack the Work Update hero-image caption on small screens
preserve full-width hero image readability without horizontal scrolling
white background
remove decorative shadows
convert header to light printable treatment
hide TOC if it wastes print space
hide milestone-next navigation
avoid breaking compact callout cards across pages when possible
render links as readable text without requiring hover
preserve code blocks and tables legibly
do not depend on background colors to preserve semantic meaning
hide the document navbar in print by default
keep the Work Update hero image and caption together when practical

styleRules: Use CSS custom properties for theme and semantic roles.
Use card hierarchy without excessive visual fragmentation.
Keep long prose comfortable to read.
Ensure code blocks and tables remain usable on narrow screens.
Preserve family resemblance with August 9 and August 15 Work Updates.
The document navbar should visually harmonize with the Work Update theme while retaining a stable recognizable placement.
The Work Update hero image container should use the day's theme colors for border/frame/caption accents without recoloring the image itself.
Near-top hero images should not exceed the main reading width and should scale fluidly on mobile.

preferredElements.nav: table of contents and explicit reading path navigation
preferredElements.article: optional nested self-contained topic where appropriate

avoid: div-only document structure when semantic elements are available
heading levels chosen only for visual size
anchor IDs generated from unstable numbering alone
inline styles repeated throughout the body when a class can express the role

identifierPresentation.firstUseRule: Pair the identifier with a semantic name or action on first meaningful appearance.
examples: WORK-0001 — Task Assignment and Tracking — Initial Project Definition

requiredChecks: HTML5 document has one doctype and one h1.
Required metadata is present.
Master-summary title/date/headline are represented accurately.
Every TOC link resolves to a unique section ID.
No substantive claim contradicts the Markdown master.
Planned future work is not presented as completed.
Historical evidence is not presented as current runtime truth.
Closed Work Units are not presented as active.
No unsupported durable IDs were invented.
Semantic colors have redundant labels.
Images have valid sources and alt text.
Wide tables and preformatted blocks are responsive.
Keyboard focus is visible.
Print view remains intelligible.
The page remains usable with JavaScript disabled.
Canonical/document URLs are not invented when unknown.
Publication state matches the sidecar.
If the HTML compresses master content, no material causal conclusion is lost.
Footer identifies the document as a downstream Work Update presentation.
The document can be opened directly from GitHub Pages or local disk.
The document navbar appears before the site header and includes the Documentation Home route.
The Documentation Home navbar target is https://sites.google.com/view/meadows-hk/home/documentation#h.fbs5hz83yg2f unless a later canonical route is explicitly established.
Navbar Contents and Top links resolve to valid internal IDs.
When a corresponding Work Update image exists, it is included near the top of main content inside the standard figure/frame container.
The Work Update image filename follows work-update-{MM-DD-YYYY}.png and its date matches the HTML Work Update date.
When HTML lives in work_updates/, the default image src is ../images/work-updates/work-update-{MM-DD-YYYY}.png unless a different verified deployment structure applies.
The Work Update hero image has informative alt text and remains responsive.
optionalChecks: Inspect at desktop and mobile widths.
Print-preview at least the first pages and one table/code section.
Verify external links used in key navigation.
Compare executive summary and resulting-state claims to sidecar/master.

publication.canonicalUrlRule: Populate only after the published GitHub Pages or other canonical URL is known.
publication.catalogRule: Catalog/listing metadata should be derived from the sidecar/publication layer after the HTML is finalized.

masterTraceability.rule: The HTML may expose a visible 'technical/source record' link to the Markdown master when published, but this should not distract from the human reading experience.

templateUseProcedure.step: Load the matching work-update sidecar when available.
Resolve the Work Update date and canonical filenames: work-update-{MM-DD-YYYY}.html and, when available, work-update-{MM-DD-YYYY}.png.
Identify the central human-facing story and 3–7 milestone reading-path points.
Choose the editorial section architecture; do not blindly mirror every Markdown section.
Create the required document navbar before the site header, linking back to the Meadows Housekeeping Documentation index and providing Contents/Top navigation.
Create header/dek/meta chips and a concise context banner when needed.

If the corresponding approved Work Update cover image exists, include ../images/work-updates/work-update-{MM-DD-YYYY}.png in the standard framed hero figure immediately after the context/source banner and before the quick-reading path.
Build the TOC and summary-stat snapshot from grounded sidecar/master facts.
Project chronology, delta, decisions, tests, and resulting state into human-readable components.
Add only additional graphics that improve understanding and have verified sources.
Apply semantic color roles redundantly with textual labels.
Validate navbar links, image filename/date/path, anchors, authority boundaries, responsive behavior, accessibility, and print behavior.
Publish only after the HTML is reviewed; then populate canonical URL/catalog metadata downstream.

templateChecks: Is the Markdown master clearly treated as authority?
Is the sidecar used as structured support rather than replacement narrative?
Does the HTML tell the day's causal story rather than merely reproduce sections?
Can the human reader follow a short reading path?
Is there a TOC for substantial updates?
Are Project/System/Resource/Work Unit roles visually and textually distinct where useful?
Are major before/after changes easy to see?
Are failures and discoveries preserved rather than polished away?
Is validation understandable without reading the full technical test matrix?
Is remaining work clearly separated from completed work?
Does the HTML remain readable on phone, desktop, and print?
Does it preserve Klinswork Work Update family resemblance while allowing subject-specific visual evolution?
Would Kevin be able to read this comfortably without needing to open the Markdown master?
Would a technical reader still be able to trace key claims back to the master/sidecar/authorities?
Does every Work Update HTML include the standard document navbar with a route back to the Documentation index?
When a dated Work Update image exists, is it included near the top in the standard framed figure container?
Does the Work Update image use the canonical work-update-{MM-DD-YYYY}.png filename and match the HTML date?
Is the image path relative and deployment-safe rather than an invented absolute URL?
